content_units: For a two-person apartment with frequent video calls and no gaming,   Plan B (300/100 for $65)   is the best value. It gives a large upload-speed boost where it matters most for calls, screen sharing, cloud backups, and simultaneous work use, without paying the premium for gigabit service you likely will not fully use.
Plan   Speed (Down/Up)   Price   Best For   Value Take
A   100/20 Mbps   $45   Light remote work, 1-2 modest calls   Cheapest, but upload is the main limitation
B   300/100 Mbps   $65   2 full-time WFH users, frequent video calls     Best overall value
C   500/20 Mbps   $70   Heavy downloading/streaming, weak upload needs   Fast download, but upload hurts WFH value
D   1000/500 Mbps   $95   Very heavy multi-user households, large file transfers   Excellent, but likely overkill for this use case
Option 1:   Plan B — 300/100 Mbps     Best balance for two remote workers with frequent video calls   High upload where it matters
-   Upload speed is the key differentiator   for your situation.
- Video calls use both download and upload, but your outgoing video, screen sharing, and file syncing depend heavily on upload.
- With   two people on simultaneous calls  ,   100 Mbps upload   is much more comfortable than   20 Mbps upload  .
- Plan B is only   $20 more than Plan A  , but gives:
- Plan C costs more than Plan B but keeps upload at only   20 Mbps  , so it is a worse fit for remote work despite the higher download number.
How Upload Speed Changes the Decision
Upload speed matters more than many people expect because home internet advertising usually emphasizes download. For your use case, that can be misleading.
-   Video meetings:   your camera feed goes upstream
-   Screen sharing:   sends a steady stream upstream
-   Cloud storage:   Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive sync upstream
-   Two simultaneous workers:   competing for the same upload pipe
- Two HD video calls can still work
- Quality may dip sooner if both people are:
- You have less headroom for spikes, and call quality is more likely to suffer first
- Screen sharing is less likely to cause stutter
- You get better stability for real-world work usage, not just speed-test bragging rights
Why Plan C loses despite faster download

Plan C gives   500 Mbps down  , which sounds stronger than Plan B’s 300 Mbps. But because it still has only   20 Mbps up  , it does not improve the part of the connection most tied to smooth work calls.
- Better upload is more valuable than extra download beyond a certain point
-   Budget pick:   Plan A, only if both residents do lighter video use and little cloud uploading
-   Premium pick:   Plan D, only if you regularly upload large files, do 4K live streaming, or want extra headroom for many devices
